skill.name: when-documenting-code-use-doc-generator
skill.description: Generates and updates code documentation, including API references, README content, inline comments, and architecture diagrams.
skill.summary: Generate project documentation from source structure, APIs, and documentation gaps.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, generated documentation placeholders, or sample configuration names. The executable slash-command scripts are real shell entry points, and the larger concern is their unpinned npx execution of claude-flow plus default writes to repository documentation files.

remediation.issue: The scripts execute claude-flow through npx using an alpha package tag.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version, document the dependency, and require explicit user confirmation before running external hooks.

remediation.issue: Documentation scripts write README and docs outputs by default.
remediation.suggestion: Make dry-run mode the default, add path allowlists, and prompt before overwriting or creating repository files.

remediation.issue: Generated examples include secret-like placeholder names such as DATABASE_URL and .env.example.
remediation.suggestion: Label all placeholders clearly and add guidance to avoid copying real secrets into generated documentation.

content.value_statement: Codebases often lack current API references, README files, comments, and diagrams. This skill analyzes project structure and produces documentation assets for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes source structure to identify functions, classes, APIs, dependencies, and documentation gaps.
Generates API documentation formats such as OpenAPI, JSDoc, TypeDoc, and Python docstrings.
Creates README content with installation, usage, configuration, testing, and contribution sections.
Adds inline documentation guidance for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Go, Rust, and C# styles.
Produces architecture and process diagrams using Mermaid or Graphviz patterns.
Provides slash-command scripts for API docs, README generation, and inline documentation reports.
limitations: Generated content should be reviewed before committing or publishing.
Route detection is heuristic and may miss custom framework patterns.
Shell scripts write documentation files in the current project and may overwrite expected outputs.
Some workflow hooks depend on external claude-flow tooling.

use_cases.title: Document a Backend API
use_cases.description: Generate OpenAPI-style references, endpoint summaries, authentication notes, and usage examples for a service repository.

use_cases.title: Refresh Project Onboarding Docs
use_cases.description: Create a README with setup, configuration, testing, contribution, and support sections from repository metadata.

use_cases.title: Improve Code Comment Coverage
use_cases.description: Identify undocumented functions and create inline comment guidance for supported language styles.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Basic Docs
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review the current repository and generate basic README and API documentation. Keep the output concise and list files changed.

prompt_templates.title: Create API Reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to document the REST API in this project. Include endpoints, request formats, response summaries, authentication notes, and validation warnings.

prompt_templates.title: Add Inline Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to find undocumented public functions in src. Add or propose JSDoc, TSDoc, or Python docstrings, and avoid changing business logic.

prompt_templates.title: Build Full Documentation Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to generate README, API reference, architecture notes, inline comment recommendations, and a documentation gap report. Run in dry-run mode when possible and flag risky writes before editing.

output_examples.input: A Node.js API project has routes but no API reference.
output_examples.output: The skill produces an API overview with endpoint summaries, authentication notes, response descriptions, and links to generated documentation files.

output_examples.input: A repository has an outdated README and missing setup instructions.
output_examples.output: The skill drafts a refreshed README with project overview, prerequisites, installation, usage, testing, configuration, and contribution sections.

output_examples.input: A source folder contains public functions without comments.
output_examples.output: The skill reports documentation coverage and proposes inline comments for functions that need parameter and return descriptions.

best_practices: Run the skill in a clean branch and review generated files before merging.
Provide the target documentation type, preferred format, and coverage goal.
Keep secrets out of examples and replace placeholders before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not run generation scripts against repositories with uncommitted critical changes.
Do not publish generated API details before checking authentication and data exposure.
Do not assume examples are production-ready without validation.

faq.question: Does this skill edit project files?
faq.answer: Yes. The included scripts can create README and docs outputs, so review changes before committing.

faq.question: Can it generate OpenAPI documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes API documentation workflows that produce OpenAPI-style references and endpoint summaries.

faq.question: Which languages are described by the skill?
faq.answer: The documentation describes JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, C#, Go, and Rust documentation styles.

faq.question: Does it validate every generated document?
faq.answer: No. It provides validation guidance, but generated content still needs human review and tool-specific checks.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Some scripts call external claude-flow tooling with npx, which can require network access if the package is not installed.

faq.question: Is it suitable for private repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. The skill scans project files and may generate documentation that exposes internal APIs or configuration names.
